## Purpose and Entry Points
PhoneInfoga is a Go-based phone-number intelligence framework: it normalizes numbers, obtains basic metadata, and runs configurable OSINT scanners. The executable starts at `main.go`; Cobra CLI commands are rooted in `cmd/root.go` and expose scan, scanner discovery, server, and version flows in `cmd/scan.go`, `cmd/scanners.go`, and `cmd/serve.go`.

## Core Domain Pipeline
The number domain layer parses, validates, and formats international phone numbers in `lib/number/number.go` and `lib/number/utils.go`. CLI or API requests pass a number into this layer, then into scanner orchestration. Filtering of scan output or scanner results is isolated in `lib/filter/filter.go`; terminal rendering is handled by `lib/output/output.go` and `lib/output/console.go`.

## Scanner Abstraction and Orchestration
`lib/remote/scanner.go` defines the scanner-facing abstraction, while `lib/remote/remote.go` coordinates scan execution and result collection. Scanner registration/initialization lives in `lib/remote/init.go`. Implementations include local lookup (`lib/remote/local_scanner.go`) and remote OSINT/search providers (`lib/remote/googlecse_scanner.go`, `lib/remote/googlesearch_scanner.go`, `lib/remote/numverify_scanner.go`, `lib/remote/ovh_scanner.go`). This boundary allows new scanners, including example plugins, without changing CLI/API callers.

## External-Service Boundary
Remote scanners call external search and number-information services. Google Custom Search and Google Search integrations are represented by `lib/remote/googlecse_scanner.go` and `lib/remote/googlesearch_scanner.go`; Numverify and OVH calls are mediated through supplier-specific interfaces in `lib/remote/suppliers/numverify.go` and `lib/remote/suppliers/ovh.go`. Supplier interfaces separate HTTP/provider behavior from scanner logic and enable mockable dependencies. API credentials and scanner selection are material runtime inputs.

## HTTP API and Server
The project can run as an HTTP service via the `serve` command. The API server is implemented in `web/v2/api/server/server.go`; request handlers for number lookup and available scanners are in `web/v2/api/handlers/numbers.go` and `web/v2/api/handlers/scanners.go`. Responses use the v2 response boundary at `web/v2/api/response.go`. Legacy/general web server and controller code remains in `web/server.go` and `web/controllers.go`; OpenAPI artifacts are published from `web/docs/swagger.yaml`.

## Browser Client
A separate Vue/TypeScript single-page client consumes the server API. Its application root is `web/client/src/main.ts`, UI composition begins in `web/client/src/App.vue`, and route-level scan/number views are in `web/client/src/views/Scan.vue` and `web/client/src/views/Number.vue`. Scanner-specific form components (`web/client/src/components/GoogleSearch.vue`, `web/client/src/components/NumverifyScan.vue`, `web/client/src/components/OVHScan.vue`) reflect backend scanner capabilities.

## Runtime and Delivery
The primary runtime is Go, distributed as a CLI, Docker image, and API server. Container packaging starts at `Dockerfile`, with local multi-service/reverse-proxy deployment variants under `support/docker/docker-compose.yml` and `support/docker/docker-compose.traefik.yml`. Release automation is configured in `.goreleaser.yml`; the web client requires its separate Node/Yarn build environment under `web/client/package.json`.
